title: Adversarial convex bandits with two values of the same function and center loss
summary: The loss sequence is fixed in advance, and every loss has the same global Lipschitz bound. Each round the algorithm submits a center and two probes and receives two exact values of the current function. Only the center incurs loss; probes may lie outside the center's feasible set.

description_paragraphs: The loss sequence is fixed in advance, and every loss has the same global Lipschitz bound. Each round the algorithm submits a center and two probes and receives two exact values of the current function. Only the center incurs loss; probes may lie outside the center's feasible set.

model.instance: The environment fixes functions $F_t:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ in advance. Each is convex and globally $L$-Lipschitz. The center satisfies $x_t\in B_2^d(R)$, while both probes may lie anywhere in $\mathbb R^d$. Feedback consists of two exact values of the same current function $F_t$.

assumptions.description: For every $t$ and all $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$, $|F_t(x)-F_t(y)|\le L\|x-y\|_2$.

model.parameter_domain_description: L: $L>0$ (public); R: $R>0$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); d: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public)
interaction_timing: The environment fixes the entire function sequence.
The learner submits a center in the ball and two probe points.
The center incurs $F_t(x_t)$, followed by the exact values at both probes.
Only received feedback may be used to select the next action.
model.adversary_information: The environment fixes the entire loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner’s private seed. This is an oblivious-adversary specification and does not automatically extend to history-dependent adaptive adversaries.
unresolved_applicability: The Gaussian random-linear hard family for the RMS sample-Lipschitz model violates a uniform per-function Lipschitz bound and cannot fill the dimension-dependent lower-bound gap in this specification.
description_paragraphs: The fixed current loss is $F_t$. Every loss is convex and globally L-Lipschitz. There are no random sample functions or observation noise.
The loss-bearing center satisfies $x_t\in B_2^d(R)$ and incurs $F_t(x_t)$.
Two probes $z_t^+,z_t^-$ of the same function are chosen together and return two exact values; they may lie outside the ball.
Require $d,T\ge1$ and $L,R>0$.
Centers lie in $B_2^d(R)$; both probes may lie in $\mathbb R^d$.

operations.query_signature: Input: $x_t\in B_2^d(R),\quad z_t^+,z_t^-\in\mathbb R^d$. The specification's protocol governs timing and visible information.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: F_t is fixed before the current action. Both probes are chosen before either current value is seen and evaluate the same F_t. No third center observation or independent Gaussian scalar error is supplied. Probes incur no additional loss; the center incurs F_t(x_t) once.

operations.coupling: F_t is fixed before the current action. Both probes are chosen before either current value is seen and evaluate the same F_t. No third center observation or independent Gaussian scalar error is supplied. Probes incur no additional loss; the center incurs F_t(x_t) once.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and explicitly permitted probes. The environment controls the current loss, outcome, or fresh sample; the learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Follow the interaction order in registry.protocols exactly. Current loss feedback follows the action; any pre-action context or advice phase is specified separately.

public_inputs: Each function is L-Lipschitz on R^d.
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
description_paragraphs: Two exact values of the same current function:

$$
x_t\in B_2^d(R),\quad z_t^+,z_t^-\in\mathbb{R}^d\ \longmapsto\ \big(F_t(z_t^+),F_t(z_t^-)\big)
$$
The function $F_t$ is fixed before the action in round $t$.
Both probes are chosen jointly before either response and access the same function $F_t$.
There is no third feedback value at the center and no independent Gaussian scalar error.
Probes incur no separate loss. The center incurs $F_t(x_t)$ once.
The quantity $d,T,L,R$ is public, and every function is $L$-Lipschitz throughout $\mathbb{R}^d$.

output.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Two values within the ball differ by at most 2LR, so the absolute cumulative comparison is at most 2LRT. Observation noise is excluded from objective-loss differences.
description_paragraphs:
$$
\mathrm{Lip}_2(F_t)\le L\quad\forall t,\qquad R_T=\sum_tF_t(x_t)-\min_{u\in B_2^d(R)}\sum_tF_t(u)
$$

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
There are T sequential rounds, each giving two exact function values, for 2T values in total.

resource.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
resource.scalarization: At fixed T, compare the native cumulative quantity in the objective. Retain the full resource vector; internal optimization, projection, and sampling are not implicitly one loss query.
resource.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
resource.online_cost: A symmetric two-point estimator and mirror descent attain the stated upper bound. On a Euclidean ball, updates can use projection. The two function calls, internal direction sampling, and projection work are recorded separately.
resource.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
resource.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real computation is permitted; feedback complexity does not imply arithmetic or bit complexity. A symmetric two-point estimator and mirror descent attain the displayed upper bound. On a Euclidean ball, projected updates are available. Charge the two function evaluations separately from direction sampling and projection.
algorithms.parallelism: Online rounds proceed sequentially. A two-point evaluation is a same-round feedback pair, not two independent rounds.
description_paragraphs: All measurable causal randomized policies respecting the stated timing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and future samples. Apart from explicit feedback, output, and budget requirements, there are no restrictions on linear spans, iteration form, internal arithmetic, memory, or communication.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{F_{1:T}}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: First take the infimum over complete nonanticipating learning policies using only public inputs.
Then take the supremum over instances fixed before interaction and satisfying the model assumptions.
Expectation includes learner randomness and any sampling or observation noise.
Fixed, per-round, and sample-path comparators are distinguished exactly as in the target expression.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
guarantees.time_uniformity: The T-round horizon is fixed and public. No anytime or simultaneous-all-T high-probability guarantee is implied.
description_paragraphs:
$$
\inf_{\mathcal{A}}\sup_{F_{1:T}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A}}[R_T]
$$

Choose one algorithm using public inputs before taking the worst case over all admissible instances. Expectation covers the algorithm's private randomness and the observation randomness specified by the model. Comparator choice and the order of summation, minimization, and expectation follow the displayed formula.

bounds.derivation: Take $f_t(x)=L\varepsilon_t x_1$. Once a center is submitted, even full revelation of the current function cannot change incurred loss. The hindsight comparator gains $LR\mathbb E|\sum_t\varepsilon_t|$. This yields a dimension-free lower bound, distinct from stronger constructions under a stochastic sample second-moment model.

notes: The source lower bound is $\Omega(L\sqrt{T(D^2+DP)})$, with path budget in $[0,TD]$. An independent one-dimensional block construction on the Euclidean ball also checks the correspondence between geometry and path length.

notes: The center $w_t$ incurs loss; the two probes in the same round provide only feedback. Multiply the source's average regret by $T$. In the random-sample variant, replace the pointwise squared Lipschitz bound with the sample Lipschitz constant's second moment.
